3. The defendant-opposite party contested the suit by filing written statements contending, inter alia, that the suit land was transferred to the plaintiff with an agreement to reconvey the suit land and accordingly the redemption case was filed and allowed by the Revenue Court. The suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 12. On perusal of the judgment and decree of the trial Court it appears that the learned Judge of the trial Court decreed the suit and declared, illegal and set-aside the judgment and decree of the Revenue Court considering the relevant provision of law under Section 95 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned appellate Court on its turn considering the materials on record, evidence, material facts and relevant provisions of law allowed the appeal and set-aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 "We are not unmindful of section 95A itself as because there is a clause that the provisions of section 95 of the Act shall apply in the case of complete usufructuary mortgage as contemplated under Section 95A. One may argue that since section 95A speaks that the provisions of section 95 will apply in such transaction, whether before or after the date of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act (Second Amendment) Order President's Order 88 of 1972; the agreement for reconveyance should be registered. But on a close examination of these two sections viz, 95 and 95A of the Act, we find, as we have stated above that this Section 95A of the Act should be considered, as far as practicable, independently and other provisions of section 95 of Act will come into play when it will be required for other ancillary matters. But as regards this agreement of reconveyance with a deed of sale, in our view, will not be required to be registered in view of the fact that in section 95A the two things namely, the deed of sale and an agreement of reconveyance shall be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage. 

 On this point we may got some light from the case of Abdul Kader vs. Abdul Aziz, 47 DLR 67. Though the factual aspects of this reported case are different, yet his Lordship, in fact, in disposing of the Reyision Case, has considered the provisions of Section 95A along with section 95(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. His Lordship expressed an opinion that an agreement for reconveyance can be specifically enforced and the provision for registration for such agreement as required under Section 95(2) of the Act is not applicable. We also hold that in a case like this. such agreement for reconveyance with a deed of sale as contemplated under Section 95A of the Act is not required to be compulsorily registered as required under sections 95(2) of the Act and, as such, the finding of the Land. Appeal Board cannot be sustained in law." 

 18. In view of the discussions, decisions and reasons stated above, I'm of the view that the impugned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below suffers from no legal infirmity which calls for no interference by this court. Thus, the Rule has no merit and is liable to be discharged.
